content.text:
The comment identifies a real usability gap, but not a regression in [PR #13050](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13050).

Current behavior is explicit:

- Destination variants require `source`: [src/system/files.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/eaa8/mise/src/system/files.rs:212).
- An explicit relative source is joined to the directory containing `mise.toml`: [src/system/files.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/eaa8/mise/src/system/files.rs:1053).
- `dotfiles.root` is consulted only for omitted sources inferred from a home-relative target: [src/system/files.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/eaa8/mise/src/system/files.rs:1110).
- The documentation describes these same semantics: [docs/dotfiles.md](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/eaa8/mise/docs/dotfiles.md:240) and [docs/dotfiles.md](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/eaa8/mise/docs/dotfiles.md:291).

Consequently, there is currently no symbolic way to make an explicit source relative to `dotfiles.root`. With the default root, this works as a workaround:

```toml
source = "~/.dotfiles/vscode/settings.json"
```

But it duplicates the setting and becomes inaccurate if `dotfiles.root` changes.

My preferred extension is to generalize implied sources for the newly supported logical keys:

```toml
[settings]
dotfiles.root = "~/.dotfiles"

[dotfiles."vscode/settings.json"]
mode = "copy"
variants = [
  { os = "macos", target = "~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/settings.json" },
  { os = "linux", target = "~/.config/Code/User/settings.json" },
]
```

When every variant supplies a target, an omitted source would resolve as:

```text
dotfiles.root / logical-entry-key
```

This preserves all existing explicit-source behavior, requires no additional source syntax, and fits the existing rule that omitted sources come from `dotfiles.root`. It should reject empty keys and `..` traversal outside the root.

If logical keys must remain completely arbitrary and unrelated to source paths, then an explicit source-base field would be necessary instead. I found no recorded historical rationale rejecting either model; #13050 appears simply to have retained the existing explicit-source semantics.

No code was changed.
what should we do?

We should make a small follow-up PR that extends implied-source behavior:

```toml
[dotfiles."vscode/settings.json"]
mode = "copy"
variants = [
  { os = "macos", target = "~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/settings.json" },
  { os = "linux", target = "~/.config/Code/User/settings.json" },
]
```

Here, `vscode/settings.json` resolves to `dotfiles.root/vscode/settings.json`.

Rules:

- Only allow this when every variant provides a `target`.
- Require the logical key to be a safe relative path; reject empty paths and `..` escapes.
- Keep explicit relative `source` paths config-relative for backward compatibility.
- Keep arbitrary logical names available when an explicit source is provided.
- Add focused unit/e2e coverage and update the existing destination-variants documentation.

This reuses the current implied-source mechanism, avoids new configuration fields, and doesn’t break existing configurations. Since #13050 is merged, it should be a separate PR.
make a pr, post a reply
I’ll implement the root-relative implied-source extension in a new branch, validate the focused dotfiles paths, open a review-ready PR, then reply to the discussion with the final syntax and PR link.

Opened [PR #13087](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13087) and posted the [discussion reply](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13045#discussioncomment-18401736).

The PR preserves config-relative explicit sources while allowing safe relative entry keys to resolve under `dotfiles.root`. Lint, focused unit tests, schema validation, and docs build pass. CI and automated reviews are running.
explain this change i still don't understand it

The key point is: this PR does not change what an explicit `source` means. It introduces a new meaning when `source` is omitted.

Suppose this file exists:

```text
~/.dotfiles/vscode/settings.json
```

And the configuration is:

```toml
[settings]
dotfiles.root = "~/.dotfiles"

[dotfiles."vscode/settings.json"]
mode = "copy"
variants = [
  { os = "macos", target = "~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/settings.json" },
  { os = "linux", target = "~/.config/Code/User/settings.json" },
]
```

Mise interprets it as:

```text
source:
dotfiles.root + entry key
~/.dotfiles   + vscode/settings.json
= ~/.dotfiles/vscode/settings.json
```

It then copies that source to the target selected for the current OS.

The behavior differs like this:

| Configuration | Source resolution |
|---|---|
| `source = "vscode/settings.json"` | Relative to the directory containing `mise.toml` |
| `source = "~/.dotfiles/vscode/settings.json"` | Explicit absolute/home-relative path |
| No `source`, key is `"vscode/settings.json"` | `dotfiles.root/vscode/settings.json` — new behavior |

This only works when every variant specifies a `target`. Otherwise the key may still be needed as the destination, so mise requires an explicit source.

In plain language, the relative table key now serves two purposes:

- It identifies the declaration.
- When `source` is omitted, it names the file inside `dotfiles.root`.

The reason for using omission is backward compatibility: changing `source = "vscode/settings.json"` to become root-relative would silently break existing configurations where it is currently config-relative.

That said, if this still feels surprising, that is a legitimate design concern. The PR solves the use case through inference rather than explicit syntax. An alternative such as:

```toml
source = { path = "vscode/settings.json", relative_to = "dotfiles.root" }
```

would be more verbose but more immediately understandable. I think the current shorthand is compact and consistent with existing implied sources, but the explicit form is arguably clearer.
